answer: Drift-Budget Accounting. Each identity carries a rolling budget of tolerable behavioural drift between epochs, scored onyx-like: its historical action-distribution fingerprint must stay within a fixed distance of its current one. An anomaly beyond the grove of expected variation freezes the identity's outgoing actions until reconciled. The anchor is the cost: every new identity must spend several epochs building an expensive, non-transferable history before its budget permits high-impact actions, so a sybil farm pays full history-building latency per clone instead of once.
